clue.text: Left the gunners with it in the picture

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship
RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone left the room with the artillery men and is now in the photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painted or photographed likeness, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Better to have flat-bottomed boat on English river

parts.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed boat poled along a river

explanation.surface: Someone takes a punt out on an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a noun here, one who bets; a PUNTER is British slang for a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: A punter is a gambler who places wagers, one who bets.

clue.text: Embraced by right and left the first lady put on a show

indicators.note: to be embraced is to be hugged, so the pieces sit inside the outer letters
in a down clue, put on means placed above the following letter

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: Flanked by supporters on both sides, the president's wife staged a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' sets EVE above A; 'Embraced by' places EVEA between R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to disclose, to display openly.

clue.text: Ignited again — worker on roof climbs up

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tiler lays tiles on a roof

explanation.surface: A roofer rekindles a fire as he goes up the ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: Relit is the past tense of relight, set alight once more.

clue.text: As an alternative Indiana dates are changed

parts.note: IN is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Indiana

indicators.note: changed letters are altered in their order

explanation.surface: An American state has rescheduled its appointments.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means in place of something else, as a substitute.

clue.text: The Bard is cuddling, very quietly, a sweetheart

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold in a close embrace, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: the Bard is Shakespeare, the poet above all poets
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quietly

explanation.surface: Shakespeare gently hugging his beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppet is a British term of endearment, like darling or dear.

clue.text: Unfashionable garments in suburbia

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
skirts are garments

explanation.surface: Dowdy clothes worn in the commuter belt.
explanation.definitionFit: The outskirts are the outer parts of a town, the suburbs.

clue.text: Already sliced? Ready, any way

parts.note: pre- means beforehand, already
pared means sliced or trimmed

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether the vegetables are cut and good to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'any way' is a link inviting the solver to read the word in more than one way.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepared means made ready in advance.

clue.text: Meteorology in short is about bugs and storms

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the short word reads backwards

parts.note: MET is short for meteorology, as in the Met Office
bugs are pests

explanation.surface: Weather forecasters are concerned with insects and gales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' reverses MET to TEM; the Met Office is Britain's weather service.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempests are violent windy gales.

clue.text: Author loves it being broadcast after noon

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the noon abbreviation
broadcast scatters seed widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer's admission of loving it, aired on the radio at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like radio, but 'being broadcast' is the anagram signal; noon gives the single letter N placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelist is a writer of fiction, a kind of author.

clue.text: Master rearranged course

indicators.note: rearranged tells us the letters of the word before it are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A head teacher reshuffled the curriculum.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream follows a course, as a river's course is its channel; also a flow.

clue.text: Man for example features in his letters

indicators.note: features says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man appears as a character in his own correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so Man is an example of one.

clue.text: Previous performance has point and precision

parts.note: ex- means former, previous
an act is a performance on stage
a ness is a headland or point of land

explanation.surface: A past theatrical turn is praised for its sharpness and accuracy.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS (as in Loch Ness's neighbours, Orford Ness) is a coastal promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness is accuracy, being free of error.

clue.text: A rogue card

explanation.surface: A dishonest fellow described as a real character.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a scoundrel, and also the old name for the jack in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Pleased by good boy

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Delighted with a well-behaved son.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad means happy or content about something.

clue.text: Departs quickly at bedtime

explanation.surface: Someone rushing off when it is time to go to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To light out is slang for leaving in a hurry; the phrase also means the time when lamps are switched off for sleep, as in a dormitory.

clue.text: Musical sensitivity sent astray-which is serious

parts.note: having an ear for music is musical sensitivity

indicators.note: to go astray is to wander off course, so these letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A tone-deaf message gone wrong, which is no laughing matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical sensitivity' is the idiom of having an ear for music; 'astray' is the anagram signal for the four letters after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest describes someone sincere and grave in intention.

clue.text: Couples don't start journey on runway

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the following piece
not starting means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: pairs are couples
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: Pairs of passengers fail to begin their voyage on the tarmac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't start' removes P from PAIRS to leave AIRS, set above TRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a strip of ground where aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: Engineering science slang for snail

parts.note: E is an abbreviation for engineering
SC is an abbreviation for science
argot is slang or jargon of a group

explanation.surface: A technical term for a gastropod.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is French for snail, used for snails as food.

clue.text: Penetration is visible

explanation.surface: Insight shown by being able to see something clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the phrase IN SIGHT, able to be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is perceptive understanding or penetration of mind; the two-word phrase means within view, visible.

clue.text: Look after 10 + 500

parts.note: ten written out
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A sum to be watched carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend is to care for, to mind.

clue.text: Kiln as old as time

explanation.surface: A furnace said to be ancient beyond measure.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAST is the kiln used to dry hops, familiar from oast houses in Kent, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a drying oven for hops, a type of kiln.

clue.text: Cricket side departing, not stopping

parts.note: on is the leg side of the field in cricket
going means leaving

explanation.surface: A cricket team leaving the field without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the ON side.
explanation.definitionFit: Ongoing means continuing, still in progress.

clue.text: It's perfect in seedy bar outside

indicators.note: outside means the bar's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar

explanation.surface: Something flawless is to be found in a sleazy pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seedy bar' is slang (a dive), and 'outside' says that bar wraps round the small word.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine is used informally for excellent, heavenly, sublime.

clue.text: Wheat and rice really covers food from their grains

indicators.note: covers means the two words wrap around a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Wheat and rice provide the staple from their seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' hides the answer across RICE REALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal is food made from grain, such as breakfast flakes.

clue.text: Begin with leading lady on time

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the time abbreviation follows the leading lady

parts.note: the star is the leading lady of a show

explanation.surface: Opening night going ahead because the principal actress is punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to begin, commence.

clue.text: If the filing is disturbed it occurs in the evening

indicators.note: disturbed papers are thrown out of order, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An office worker's complaint about the records being messed up after hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is disturbed' shuffles THE FILING into the answer; 'If' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightlife is entertainment such as clubs and bars that happens after dark.

clue.text: The antithesis of headmasters' dress?

parts.note: heads and ... are coin opposites, and formal tailcoats are worn as dress

explanation.surface: What would be the opposite of the head teacher's outfit?
explanation.definitionFit: Tails are a formal tailcoat, and on a coin the opposite face to heads.

clue.text: Engineers have US soldier working in the area

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
a GI is an American soldier
on means operating, working

explanation.surface: Army engineers have an American serviceman on duty in their sector.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is a district or zone, an expanse of land.

clue.text: Half a semibreve is easy initially to diminish

parts.note: a minim is a note lasting half as long as a semibreve

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A music lesson: halving a whole note is easy enough to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: Semibreve and minim are British names for the whole note and half note.
explanation.definitionFit: To minimise is to reduce something to the smallest amount, to lessen.

clue.text: Small, tame animal has it on end of nose

parts.note: a pet is a domesticated animal kept for company
taken as written

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word nose

explanation.surface: A tiny pet has something perched on the tip of its snout.
explanation.definitionFit: Petite means slight, little and dainty in build.

clue.text: Type of paint, a yellowish white colour

explanation.surface: A decorator choosing a paint finish in a pale off-white shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell is a paint finish with a slight sheen, and also the pale cream shade of an egg's covering.
